dedupe_keys.name: tees valley traffic digital twin region wide automated signal control for traffic and bus reliability 2025

description: This case describes the first phase of a region-wide traffic digital twin in the Tees Valley, north-east England, that detects disruption and changes traffic signal strategies automatically to cut delays for general traffic and buses. The Tees Valley Combined Authority led it within its Digital Transport Programme, with Middlesbrough Council's urban traffic management team as operational lead and Aimsun and Yunex Traffic as delivery partners. The system uses Aimsun Live, which combines machine-learning traffic data models, real-time data integration and a high-fidelity simulation model to give historical, live and one-hour predictive views of the network, fed by urban traffic control systems, VivaCity sensors, street works data and the National Traffic Information Service. It is integrated with Yunex Stratos and UTC-UX to actuate pre-tested signal strategies, with an incident detection module and a bus reliability module, uses DATEX II and runs in the cloud. Coverage is the Tees Valley road network. The project report of November 2025 is free to read online; the model and data are not public. Outcome: monitoring from July to September 2025 found a 13.7% cut in average travel time for general traffic where strategies were deployed (simulation based) and a mean gain of 11.6 mph in bus segment speeds within 15 minutes of activation (on-street data). Limitations: results are preliminary, data quality and integration caused delays, and a 12-month evaluation follows. The case shows operational control of a regional road and bus network with a data-assimilating twin.
